t: You're outside The Edmund Halley, a pub in London. It's named after Edmond Halley, the English astronomer, mathematician and physicist. Halley became the second Astronomer Royal in 1720, succeeding John Flamsteed. That's about all the record tells me, but it explains the name: a pub that borrows its title from one of Britain's best-known men of science, who lived from 1656 to 1742.
